title: Build a Bilingual HubSpot AI Chatbot With One Knowledge Base
summary: Connect HubSpot live chat to Quickchat AI. Set up a shared inbox, test one knowledge base update in English and French, and hand a chat to a teammate.
body_markdown:
Beacon Bench just made room on its shelf for three extra days. Customers used to have seven calendar days to collect a repaired lamp. The shop changed one number on its English pickup page, the only article in its Quickchat AI knowledge base. The rule now gives customers **10 calendar days after the shop sends the ready-for-collection email** . Here’s what two visitors saw when they asked about the deadline in **HubSpot live chat** .


English. The ten days start when the shop sends the ready-for-collection email. Weekends count.


French. « À compter de l’envoi » keeps the same starting point. The visitor also learns which reference to bring.


You’ll build this withone English knowledge base article anda HubSpot chatflow . First, capture theseven-day answers . Thenpublish the ten-day rule and see which details carry over. A third visitor asked how much it would cost to ship a lamp to Corsica. The article had no price.Follow that conversation into the workshop’s inbox to see Piotr pick it up and the visitor answer him in French.


## 1. How do you give the chatbot one English policy?


The source for our fictional lamp shop is a HubSpot landing page. A customer can read the collection rule, check what to bring, and open live chat on the same screen.


We opened the published page signed out. The green chat launcher greeted us with “How can we help with your repair?”


The screenshots use the English interfaces in both apps. Copy these two English sentences onto a page you can edit and keep the visitor questions in the languages shown. Later you’ll change the deadline and use the repair reference to check that the other detail survived.


> **Collecting a repaired lamp**
>
>
> Beacon Bench holds your repaired lamp for 7 calendar days after we send the ready-for-collection email.
>
>
> Bring the repair reference from your email when you collect your lamp.


**Choose your HubSpot portal.** If you already have a practice portal with the seats you need, use it for both the page and its chatflow. To create a developer test account, sign in to HubSpot with your existing login or create a free one. Open **Development** (under **More** if your sidebar is condensed), then **Testing → Test Accounts → Create developer test account** . Name it **Beacon Bench** , leave **Customize my test account** unchecked and click **Create** . When the list shows **Active** , click **Beacon Bench** . Check the account name in the top-right corner before changing any settings.[Free HubSpot signup](https://app.hubspot.com/signup-hubspot/crm) ·[HubSpot test accounts](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/getting-started/account-types)


*The form defaults to Enterprise for all Hubs. We used that default for the Beacon Bench trial.*


1. **Make your own copy of the policy.** Use a public page you can edit. In the HubSpot portal you just chose, open **Content → Landing Pages** and use **Create** to start a blank page. When you see **Untitled** and **Draft** , the page already exists.


**Add the policy.** Click the pencil beside **Untitled** and name the draft **Collecting a repaired lamp** . Click the blue **+ Add section** in the middle of the page. Under **Blank layouts** , choose the tile labeled **2** . Two areas marked **Drop modules here** appear. Use the **+** on the far left to drag **Rich text** into the left column. Replace the placeholder with the heading and both sentences. Select just the first line and choose **Heading 1** in the text toolbar.[HubSpot’s drag-and-drop editor](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/website-pages/edit-page-content-in-a-drag-and-drop-area)


Put the policy in the **Rich text** module in the left column.


**Add the lamp.** From the same **+** menu, drag **Image** into the right column. Select the module and click the image placeholder in the left sidebar. In the **Select image** panel, click **Upload** at the bottom. Once the lamp appears under **Recently updated** , click its thumbnail to place it beside the policy.[Workshop lamp photo](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/beacon-bench/workshop-lamp.webp)


Click the placeholder in the **Image** module to choose the lamp photo for the right column.


The diagram on tile 2 gives the text and photo equal space. The thumbnail under Recently updated is the image you can place on the page.


**Publish and check the address.** Click the **Settings** gear below **Preview** . Set **Page title** to **Collecting a repaired lamp | Beacon Bench** . Under **Page URL** , choose your test domain and enter` lamp-collection` as the **Content slug** . Save, check **Preview** , then return to the editor and click **Publish** . Our confirmation said **Nicely done** and showed a **Copy** button beside the public URL. Open that address signed out and check both sentences. You’ll use the same address for the import.[Sample pickup page](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/beacon-bench/lamp-collection.html) ·[HubSpot’s page settings](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/website-and-landing-pages/create-and-customize-pages)


Set the browser tab title in **Page title** . Quickchat AI uses it to name the imported article.


After **Nicely done** appears, copy the published address. Open it while signed out of HubSpot.


1. **Create the Agent.** In the[Quickchat AI dashboard](https://app.quickchat.ai/register) , choose **Set up manually** in Getting Started. Under **Identity** , name it **Beacon Bench Support** . A personal test can use the Free plan. Live replies and test runs use AI credits, and commercial use starts at Starter.[Quickchat AI plans](https://quickchat.ai/docs/pricing-and-plans)
2. **Import only this page.** In **Knowledge Base → Add Website → Single Page** , enter the published page address. Expand **Advanced options** and check **HTML selector** . We entered` main .hs-elevate-rich-text` for the HubSpot page. For the downloadable sample, use` #pickup-policy` . Click **Import** . When **Adding Knowledge** finishes, open the new **URL** row marked **Ready** .


Choose **Add Website** to import the policy from its published address.


In the import dialog, the selector picks out the policy from the rest of the landing page.


Our URL article took its title, **Collecting a repaired lamp | Beacon Bench** , from the browser tab. Under **Content** , it held just the page heading and the two sentences a visitor reads. The email that starts the clock was there. The navigation and footer were gone.


When you add more policies, the[chatbot knowledge base guide](https://quickchat.ai/post/chatbot-knowledge-base-guide) shows how to organize articles and catch conflicting answers.


If you first pasted the policy by hand, you’ll see two **Ready** rows. Keep the row with type **URL** and the published address. The older **Collecting a repaired lamp** row has type **Article** and an empty URL cell. Once you’ve verified the imported text, open the older row’s **… → Delete** , check its title, and confirm. That gives the seven-day rule one place to change in step 4.


Keep the **URL** entry. It is the one you can refresh when the page changes.


Inside the saved article, both the deadline and the repair reference survived the import.


1. **Set the languages.** In **Identity → AI Persona → Languages** , put **English** first and add **French** . A complete French sentence gives the Agent a clear language signal. For an ambiguous opening such as “OK”, the first language is the fallback. Set **Creativity** to **Low** .[Language and creativity settings](https://quickchat.ai/docs/ai-agent/identity)


*English is the fallback. French visitors can ask about the same English article.*


In **Identity → Main Prompt** , paste the instructions below. Keep the deadline in the article so a policy edit has just one source of truth.


```text
You are Beacon Bench Support. Help visitors collect a repaired lamp.
Answer questions about shop policy using the Knowledge Base. Reply in the visitor's language and preserve quantities, units and conditions from the article.
If the article does not cover the question, say which detail you lack and offer to connect the visitor to a person.
```


Save, open **AI Preview** , and ask **“How long do I have to collect my repaired lamp, and when does the clock start?”** Our seven-day reply opened with “You have 7 calendar days, starting when we send the ready-for-collection email.” If your reply counts from drop-off, open the stored article and check the wording there.


**Working without a public page?** In **Knowledge Base → Add Article** , save the same title and two sentences and wait for **Ready** . In step 4, edit that article directly. The four visitor replies on the published HubSpot page in this walkthrough use the URL article. If your team already publishes in HubSpot’s own knowledge base, you can import the published article’s reader URL. HubSpot’s article editor has its own seat and subscription requirements. Keep just one copy of the policy in the Agent.[HubSpot’s knowledge base requirements](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/knowledge-base/create-and-customize-knowledge-base-articles)


## 2. How do you route HubSpot live chat to this Agent?


HubSpot assigns the visitor’s thread to a dedicated user, **Beacon Bot** . Quickchat AI matches that user’s email and replies in the same thread. A second user takes over questions that need the workshop. In our portal, that was **Piotr** , signed in with his own HubSpot account.


*Open the conversation in HubSpot to see who owns it. Open the matching reply in Quickchat AI to see which article the Agent used.*


1. **Check your routing seats.** Open **Settings → Users & Teams → Seats** inside the test portal. HubSpot requires an assigned **Sales Seat** or **Service Seat** for the person setting up automatic routing and for the user receiving chats. The seat cards show what the portal provides. The table below them shows who has each assignment.[Seat types](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/account-management/manage-seats) ·[Automatic routing requirements](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/inbox/set-your-conversations-routing-rules)


*Both counts of 1 belonged to the same operator. With unlimited trial seats in these two categories, we could give Beacon Bot its own qualifying seat.*


1. **Invite Beacon Bot.** Keep your own login for the human side of the conversation. In **Users & Teams → Users → Add users → Create new** , enter a second email address you control, assign one available **Service Seat** or **Sales Seat** , and send the invitation. Accept it in a separate browser profile. While signed in as that user, open the top-right account menu and choose **Profile & Preferences → General → Profile** . Enter **Beacon** as the first name and **Bot** as the last name, then click **Save** . Back in your operator browser, check that **Users & Teams → Users** lists Beacon Bot as active with its seat. Keep the bot’s email address for the Quickchat AI connection.[Add a HubSpot user](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/account-management/add-hubspot-users) ·[Edit a HubSpot profile](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/user-management/profile-and-preferences)


Assign the bot user a routing seat. This test portal offered **Service Enterprise Seat** .


1. **Set up the shared inbox.** Open **Settings → Inbox & Help Desk → Inboxes** . If HubSpot shows **Create your inbox** , choose **Create General inbox** , the button on the right. This gives the bot and the workshop a shared conversation thread. The **Help Desk inbox** option turns incoming requests into tickets. On **Create team inbox** , enter **Beacon Bench Support** in **Team inbox name** . Leave **Available to everyone** selected in this two-user test portal, click **Next** , then choose **Chat** when HubSpot offers channels.


*Both users need inbox access so a person can pick up the thread. The chatflow’s assignment setting decides who gets the first message.*


If HubSpot opens an existing Conversations Inbox, use it. On its **Access** tab, check that Beacon Bot and your operator both have access. Choose **Connect a channel → Chat** if needed. In **Settings → Inbox & Help Desk → Availability Management** , set Beacon Bot to **Available** so it can receive chats when routing uses availability.[HubSpot inbox setup](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/inbox/set-up-the-conversations-inbox) ·[User availability](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/inbox/manage-your-inbox-users)


1. **Connect chat to the lamp page.** In the channel wizard, select **Web** . This covers people browsing the page on a laptop or phone. On **Display** , set the widget color to` #344F41` to match the green desk lamp on the demo page. We kept the default **System-UI** font.[HubSpot’s chat channel wizard](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/inbox/connect-and-customize-a-chat-channel-in-the-conversations-inbox)


*Choose Chat when HubSpot asks what to connect, then Web when it asks where visitors will use it. The Mobile option embeds chat inside a native app.*


1. **Set the welcome visitors will see.** On **Availability** , choose **Based on chat operating hours** and check **Chat is available 24/7** for the test portal. On **Chatflow** , enter “How can we help with your repair?” as the welcome message. Under **Chat heading** , we chose **Specific users and teams → Beacon Bot** . HubSpot displayed the user’s first name, **Beacon** , above the greeting. If you prefer the shop name, choose **Custom branding** and enter **Beacon Bench Support** . Leave the option to use that branding throughout the conversation unchecked so a teammate can appear under their own name at handoff.


*These hours keep the widget open. The greeting is visible before the visitor asks a question or the Agent sends a reply.*


Turn on **Automatically assign conversations** and check the greeting in **Preview** . At **Install code** , choose **Skip & verify** if you’re using a landing page hosted in this HubSpot portal. HubSpot already includes its tracking code on that page. If the demo page is on another host, install the test portal’s snippet there.[HubSpot tracking code](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/reports/install-the-hubspot-tracking-code)


*The desktop preview shows the repair greeting. HubSpot then confirms that new threads will reach the inbox. Open the saved chatflow to see who will receive them.*


1. **Check who receives the chat.** Open **Service → Chatflows → Web Chat** . In our portal, the wizard created an enabled flow named **Live Chat** with **Beacon Bench Support** in the Inbox column. Hover over that row and click **Edit** . The preview already said **Beacon** , but when we opened **Chat → Assignment** , HubSpot still had the human operator selected. Under **Assign to → Specific users and teams** , remove the operator, select **Beacon Bot** as the sole recipient, then click **Save** at the bottom left. If **Assign to available users only** is checked, open **Manage team availability** and make sure Beacon Bot is **Available** .[HubSpot’s live chat controls](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/chatflows/create-a-live-chat)


Open **Chatflows** from **Service** to edit the flow that routes the chat.


When routing depends on availability, use **Manage team availability** to check the bot’s status.


On **Target** , set **Website URL** to match the published demo page. Save and turn the chatflow on. If you can see the widget in Preview but the published page has no launcher, compare the actual URL with the targeting rule, check the availability hours, and verify the tracking code if the page is hosted outside HubSpot.[Troubleshoot a missing chat widget](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/chatflows/chat-widget-is-not-appearing-on-your-pages)


If your site uses Quickchat AI’s own widget, the[website chatbot installation guide](https://quickchat.ai/post/add-chatgpt-to-your-website) covers the installation snippet and mobile checks.


If you’re reusing an inbox and the **Web Chat** list is empty, choose **Create chatflow → Website** , select that inbox, then **English** for the widget and **Live agent** . If **Enable Knowledge Base search** appears, leave it off. It adds a separate article search box for visitors. Then set assignment and targeting as above.


*The reference screen shows the default “is all pages”. Replace it with an exact match for your published test page before turning on the chatflow.*


1. **Authorize Quickchat AI from the operator’s browser.** Open HubSpot’s top-right account menu and check that your operator is signed in to **Beacon Bench** . In that same browser, open the Beacon Bench Support Agent in Quickchat AI as an Editor, Administrator or Account Owner. Go to **External Apps → HubSpot → Connect to HubSpot** . Enter **Beacon Bot’s email** in **HubSpot User Email** . Click **Connect to HubSpot** again and select **Beacon Bench → Choose Account** . Review the requested access and app terms, then click **Connect app** . The operator approves the installation. Quickchat AI uses the dedicated user’s email to identify which conversations the Agent should answer.[Quickchat AI’s HubSpot setup guide](https://quickchat.ai/post/create-ai-chatbot-for-hubspot)


Open HubSpot in **External Apps** , read the prerequisites, then choose **Connect to HubSpot** .


Enter the address that belongs to **Beacon Bot** in **HubSpot User Email** .


Approve the app from the operator’s account and choose **Connect app** .


Our first attempt stopped at **Request permissions to connect** . HubSpot listed **Account Access** and **CRM Property Settings Editor** . We retried from the browser where the test portal’s **Super Admin** was signed in, entered Beacon Bot’s existing email in Quickchat AI, and approved the app in HubSpot. Back in Quickchat AI, the panel showed **Connected** and **Enabled** . A user with **App Marketplace access** can also install the app if they have the permissions it requests.[HubSpot’s app installation requirements](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/marketplace/install-apps-in-the-hubspot-marketplace)


Both screens refer to Beacon Bot. Use that user’s email in the Quickchat AI dialog and save its assignment in HubSpot.


HubSpot asked the operator for permission to read and send conversation messages. The two green badges appeared in Quickchat AI after the operator approved access.


1. **Try the chat as a customer.** In HubSpot, return to **Service → Chatflows → Web Chat** . Hover over **Live Chat** , click **Edit → Preview** , and ask **“How long do I have to collect my repaired lamp, and when does the clock start?”** Leave the preview open.[Test the HubSpot channel](https://quickchat.ai/docs/channels/hubspot#answer-live-chat-with-a-hubspot-chatflow)


HubSpot first offered to follow up by email. We left the field empty. Beacon gave us **7 calendar days** from when the shop sends the ready-for-collection email and reminded us to bring our repair reference. For this first test, the Agent used the seven-day article we had entered by hand. Here’s how the same exchange appeared on each side of the chat.


Visitor view. The blank field is for the visitor’s address. Beacon counts from the email the shop sends when the lamp is ready.


Operator view. HubSpot labels the email prompt **Automated** . The pickup answer is signed **Beacon Bot** , the owner shown above the thread.


To change when the email prompt appears, open **Chat → Personalize → Email capture** in the chatflow editor. Under **Ask visitors for their email address** , choose the timing and edit the invitation.[HubSpot’s live chat settings](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/chatflows/create-a-live-chat#build-live-chat)


When we returned the next morning, **All open** showed only **Maria Johnson (Sample Contact)** . We found our English preview under **More → All closed → Unknown Visitor** . HubSpot recorded the assignment to **Beacon Bot** at 10:25 PM and the thread closing at 10:36 PM. If several threads say **Unknown Visitor** , click the magnifying glass beside the inbox name and search for` repaired lamp` across open and closed conversations.[HubSpot’s inbox views and controls](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/inbox/use-the-conversations-inbox)


If a test thread has disappeared from the open list, look under **All closed** .


Search for a phrase from the test message, then open the matching **Unknown Visitor** thread.


## 3. What should the English and French visitors see?


Open the published pickup page for this test. Keep the widget language set to English throughout. The French visitor’s own message is the cue to answer in French.


1. Open the targeted page in a private browser session, open the widget, and send the English question below. Read the answer **in the widget** .
2. In your **operator’s browser** , open **CRM → Inbox** . Click the inbox name above your availability at the top left, choose **Beacon Bench Support** , then click **All open** . Open the lamp conversation and read **Owner** above the messages. It should show **Beacon Bot** . The **Contact owner** in the right sidebar belongs to the visitor’s CRM record.
3. Close **all** Chrome Incognito windows to end the English visitor’s session, or open a private window in a different browser. Visit the same page and ask the French question. Check that the chat starts with the welcome message and that HubSpot records a separate conversation. Save the first French reply before asking what to bring.[How Chrome handles Incognito sessions](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95464?hl=en)
4. Open the matching conversation in the Quickchat AI **Inbox** . In our HubSpot thread, a team-only comment included the URL for that transcript. Leave the transcript set to **Original** and open **Why AI said that** beneath the answer. Inspect the retrieved article and the passage about collection. This lets you trace a wrong number back to the text that supplied it.[Inspect a Quickchat AI reply](https://quickchat.ai/docs/conversations/inbox)


Send this exact message What to check


How long do I have to collect my repaired lamp, and when does the clock start? Seven **calendar** days from when the shop sends the ready email.


De combien de temps est-ce que je dispose pour récupérer ma lampe réparée, et à partir de quand ? The same interval and starting event in French. “Sept jours ouvrés” would give the customer extra time.


Que dois-je apporter pour récupérer ma lampe ? The repair reference from the email. The source asks for nothing else.


On November 20, 2026, we tested the pickup deadline in the published HubSpot chat. The first two visitors asked before the shop changed its policy. Both chat bubbles give seven calendar days from the ready email.


English. The clock starts when the shop sends the email.


French. « À partir de l’envoi » keeps the same starting point.


On the published page, the greeting and the email prompt stayed in English. The French visitor left the field empty and got “Vous disposez de 7 jours calendaires à partir de l’envoi de l’e-mail vous informant que votre lampe est prête.” Beacon volunteered the repair reference in its first reply to both visitors. In Quickchat AI **Inbox** , we opened two separate HubSpot conversations in **Original** view and matched each question and answer to the visitor’s screen.


If you also want a French greeting, edit the welcome message and email prompt in a French chatflow and target it to your French pages. You can assign that flow to the same dedicated HubSpot user.[HubSpot chatflow language settings](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/chatflows/edit-your-chatflows-language-settings)


For other language pairs, the[multilingual chatbot guide](https://quickchat.ai/post/multilingual-chatbots) shows how to test language detection, widget text and the facts in a reply separately.


*The widget is the customer’s view. Open the matching reply in the Quickchat AI Inbox to find **Why AI said that** . Save the seven-day answers before you change the source.*


## 4. How do you change the deadline in both languages?


The shop has found room on its pickup shelf for three more days. Edit **one number** on the original page, then make two new customers ask about it.


1. Reopen the same source page. In HubSpot, go to **Content → Landing Pages** , select **Collecting a repaired lamp** , and click inside the policy text. Change **7 calendar days** to **10 calendar days** . Click **Update** . When HubSpot says **Your page is updated** , open the published URL signed out and read the sentence there.
2. In the Quickchat AI Knowledge Base, open the **URL** article. In **Metadata** , click **Refresh URL Manually** . The control sits below **Auto-refresh** in our account. With no unsaved edits in the article, wait for the refresh to finish and read the updated body in the open editor. Check the number, the event that starts the clock, and the repair reference. If you wrote the article directly in Quickchat AI, edit and save the number there.[How article refresh works](https://quickchat.ai/docs/ai-agent/knowledge-base)


During our test, we reopened the article after the first refresh and the saved rule still said **7** . The public page already said **10** . We refreshed the URL article a second time and confirmed the saved rule now said **10** . That fetch also brought in the lamp image and the chat greeting. Read what the refresh stored, even if you used an HTML selector for the initial import.


From the page editor to the saved article. In each application, read the policy sentence itself.


This refresh also imported the lamp photo. Check what the saved article contains after you refresh it.


1. Open two fresh visitor sessions on the published page. Repeat theoriginal English and French questions . We left the native email prompt blank, as before. Both visitors got the replies at the top of this guide, and we matched each one to its HubSpot conversation in the Quickchat AI Inbox.


Under **All** , use the language and deadline in the reply preview to find the right conversation.


Open **Why AI said that** under the answer whose source you want to check.


What the visitor learned in live HubSpot chat Before the edit After the edit


English pickup window 7 calendar days 10 calendar days


French pickup window 7 jours calendaires 10 jours calendaires


When the clock starts, in both languages When the shop sends the ready email When the shop sends the ready email


What to bring Repair reference from the email Repair reference from the email


**If a fresh chat still quotes seven** , look at the published page, the stored article and the passage under **Why AI said that** , in that order. A **Refresh failed** status leaves the previous version available. A duplicate article can also supply the old number. For recurring changes, paid plans offer daily automatic URL refresh.


Here is what a source check looks like in a separate **Quickchat AI Preview** run. The visitor asked in French. The Agent searched in English for` repaired lamp collection deadline starting notification` and retrieved the English paragraph with the ten-day rule.


*The source passage lets the shop check the number and the condition that came with it.*


**Keep the test for the next policy change.** In **Conversations → Testing → Create Dataset → Paste messages** , paste the[three test questions](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/beacon-bench/pickup-questions.txt) . They’re already separated by` ---` on its own line. Name the dataset **Beacon pickup** . Set the evaluation criterion to “Reply in the visitor’s language. Give the number of calendar days and the event that starts the clock. For collection, give the repair reference from the email.” Name each run for its source version, review the credit cost, then run it and inspect the individual answers. Use the HubSpot widget to check that the visitor actually receives the reply.[Quickchat AI Testing](https://quickchat.ai/docs/conversations/testing)


If you manage your Agent from ChatGPT or Claude, connect Quickchat AI, paste the three questions and ask, “In Beacon Bench Support, create a test dataset named Beacon pickup using these three visitor messages. Show me the saved messages so I can check them before starting a run.” HubSpot sign-in and chatflow assignment take place in the portal.[Quickchat AI for ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a4656c688748191be4c5247fb0d5dfc) ·[Quickchat AI for Claude](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/app-quickchat-ai)


## 5. Who answers when the customer asks about shipping to Corsica?


The article tells customers how to collect a lamp. It says nothing about sending one to Corsica. Leave those two sentences alone. This last visitor will need somebody at the workshop.


1. In **Actions & MCPs → Human Handoff** , turn the Action on and open **Edit Action** . Enable the **Lack Of Knowledge** rule. To isolate this case in the demo, switch off other rules and leave the keyword list empty. Leave **Human Agents’ availability** off for the test.[Human Handoff settings](https://quickchat.ai/docs/ai-agent/actions/human-handoff)


*With this rule enabled on its own, the first shipping question tests how the Agent handles a gap in the article.*


1. Open **External Apps → HubSpot → Settings** . Our connected Agent already had **Support Pipeline** selected for tickets created both during and outside working hours. Leave both selections in place for this test. With **Human Agents’ availability** off, Quickchat AI uses the during-working-hours selection.[Handoff tickets in HubSpot](https://quickchat.ai/docs/channels/hubspot#handoff-tickets)


*The handoff ticket gives the workshop a record of the shipping question. Open the associated conversation to send the visitor a reply.*


1. Return to the French visitor’s widget on the lamp page. If the message box is still open, continue there. When we came back to our ten-day reply, HubSpot showed **“Your chat has ended.”** Select the green **“To start a new chat, click here.”** link if you see that notice.


*The link below the last reply starts a new conversation.*


1. In the visitor tab, ask **“Pouvez-vous expédier ma lampe réparée en Corse et combien cela coûte-t-il ?”** The visitor wants to know whether the workshop can ship a repaired lamp to Corsica and what it would cost. Keep the tab open. In our fresh chat, Beacon’s first reply was “Je ne peux pas confirmer l’expédition en Corse ni son coût. Je vous mets en relation avec un membre de notre équipe.”


*HubSpot opened the handoff ticket at 4:44 PM (Warsaw time). The visitor added “Oui, je voudrais parler à quelqu’un” at 4:45 PM. By then, somebody at the workshop could already pick up the question.*


1. In a second browser profile, sign in to HubSpot **as the human operator** . Open **CRM → Inbox → Beacon Bench Support → All open** . Select the conversation with **Corse** in the visitor’s message. On the right, our associated ticket was already **New (Support Pipeline)** . Above the conversation, **Owner** still said **Beacon Bot** . Open that dropdown and select your own name.


Choose your own name under **Owner** when you take over the conversation.


Piotr took ownership of the conversation at 4:46 PM. The ticket still belonged to Beacon Bot. You can follow up on the ticket separately from replying to the person waiting in chat.


1. Below the messages, select **Live Chat** , type **“Je vais vérifier les possibilités d’envoi avec l’atelier.”** and click **Send** . The adjacent **Comment** tab writes a private note for colleagues. Switch back to the visitor tab. The header now says **Piotr** , and the visitor can read his promise to check with the workshop. As the visitor, send **“Merci, j’attends votre réponse.”** Look for that line back in the same HubSpot inbox thread.


To reply to the visitor, use **Live Chat** . Write private team notes under **Comment** .


At 4:47 PM the visitor and Piotr could read each other’s messages in the original chat. The workshop still owed the customer a shipping answer.


Keep all three questions for the next policy change. The two pickup questions tell you whether both languages carry the new deadline, its starting point and the repair reference. The Corsica question tells you whether the person who needs an answer can actually reach somebody who can get it.


To see what the visitor hears when nobody is on duty, follow the[human handoff walkthrough for staffed and unstaffed hours](https://quickchat.ai/post/chatbot-human-handoff-workflow) .


## Frequently asked questions


### How do I connect a knowledge base to a HubSpot chatbot?


In Quickchat AI, choose Knowledge Base → Add Website → Single Page, import the public article URL and wait for Ready. In External Apps → HubSpot, connect the dedicated HubSpot user and select that same user under Chat → Assignment in the HubSpot chatflow. HubSpot’s Enable Knowledge Base search setting adds a visitor-facing article search box. The Quickchat AI import supplies the article used in replies.


### Can a HubSpot chatbot answer in French from an English knowledge base?


Yes. Route HubSpot live chat to a Quickchat AI Agent, import the English article and add French in its language preferences. On our published pickup page, changing seven days to ten produced “10 calendar days” in English and “10 jours calendaires” in French. Both visitors also learned when the clock starts and which reference to bring.


### Do I need a HubSpot knowledge base subscription to use my help articles?


A public landing page works as a source for a Quickchat AI Single Page import. We imported our English pickup policy from a HubSpot-hosted page and checked that the Ready URL article contained both policy sentences. You can also paste the text into a Quickchat AI article. Publishing to HubSpot’s own knowledge base requires Service Hub Professional or Enterprise and the relevant seat and publishing access.


### How do I import just the policy text from a HubSpot landing page?


In Quickchat AI’s Single Page import, open Advanced options and enable HTML selector. Choose the element containing your policy, then check the text stored in the Ready URL article. Our HubSpot template used main .hs-elevate-rich-text. The downloadable sample uses #pickup-policy. Check the stored text again after a manual refresh.


### Can I test HubSpot live chat without changing my company’s website?


Yes. Use a practice portal with routing seats, or sign in with your existing HubSpot login and open Development → Testing → Test Accounts → Create developer test account. Once the test account is Active, publish a page under Content → Landing Pages and set the chatflow’s Website URL rule to match only that page.


### Which HubSpot seats do I need for automatic live chat routing?


The person configuring automatic routing and the HubSpot user receiving the chats each need an assigned Sales Seat or Service Seat. Our developer test account included unlimited Sales Enterprise and Service Enterprise trial seats. In Settings → Users & Teams → Seats, check which user holds each seat before assigning the chatflow.


### Should I choose a General inbox or a Help Desk inbox for HubSpot live chat?


For this walkthrough, choose Create General inbox under Settings → Inbox & Help Desk → Inboxes. Give the dedicated user and the teammate access, then connect Chat → Web. A General inbox lets them work in the same thread under CRM → Inbox. HubSpot’s Help Desk manages incoming requests as tickets.


### How do I change the name visitors see in the HubSpot chat widget?


In the chatflow, open Chat heading. Choose Specific users and teams to display a user, or Custom branding to display the shop name. To change the user’s own name, sign in as that user and edit Profile & Preferences → General → Profile. Leave persistent branding off if you want visitors to see the teammate’s name at handoff.


### Why does HubSpot say I don’t have permission to install Quickchat AI?


HubSpot checks the permissions of the person approving the app. Our first attempt listed Account Access and CRM Property Settings Editor. We signed in to the test portal as a Super Admin, restarted the connection from Quickchat AI with the dedicated chat user’s email, and approved the app in HubSpot. Quickchat AI then showed Connected and Enabled.


### Why does HubSpot live chat work in Preview but disappear on my website?


In Service → Chatflows, check that the flow is on. Under Target, compare the website URL rule with the address a visitor actually opens. Check the channel’s availability hours. A page hosted outside HubSpot needs the tracking code from the connected portal. HubSpot already includes that code on pages hosted in the portal.


### Why is my HubSpot chatbot silent when a new chat arrives?


Open the visitor’s thread in HubSpot and check its owner. Chat heading controls the name visitors see. Under Chat → Assignment, new conversations must go to the dedicated user whose email is saved in Quickchat AI. Check the user’s inbox access, routing seat and availability, then try a fresh chat on the targeted page.


### Why does HubSpot live chat ask for an email address before my chatbot replies?


HubSpot’s Email capture setting controls when the chat widget asks for a visitor’s address. In our test, we left the field blank and the Agent answered in the same chat. To change the timing or wording, open the chatflow’s Chat tab and expand Email capture under Personalize.


### Why is my HubSpot chat greeting in English when the chatbot replies in French?


HubSpot controls the welcome message and email prompt. Quickchat AI uses the visitor’s message to choose the reply language. For a French greeting on French pages, create a French chatflow, edit the messages under Chat → Personalize and target those page URLs. You can route it to the same dedicated user and keep one English policy article.


### Where can I find a HubSpot test chat that disappeared from All open?


Open CRM → Inbox and select the inbox used by the chatflow. Check More → All closed. An anonymous test visitor can appear as Unknown Visitor. Use the magnifying glass beside the inbox name to search for a distinctive phrase from the chat, such as repaired lamp, across open and closed threads.


### How do I update both languages after a policy change?


Publish the change on the original page. Open its URL article in Quickchat AI and click Refresh URL Manually. Once it shows Ready, check the stored wording and ask the same question in two fresh HubSpot chats, one per language. For an article written directly in Quickchat AI, edit the article itself.


### Why does my chatbot still give the old answer after I refresh a URL article?


Open the published page signed out and check the number there first. After the refresh finishes, read the number in the URL article. If the public page has the new number and the saved article still has the old one, refresh the article again. If the article is current, start a fresh chat and open Why AI said that beneath the reply to see which source supplied the answer.


### How can a teammate take over a HubSpot chatbot conversation?


Enable Human Handoff and its Lack Of Knowledge rule in Quickchat AI. When a visitor asks a question the article cannot answer, the Agent can hand it off and create a HubSpot ticket. In CRM → Inbox, open the conversation, choose your name under Owner and reply from Live Chat. In our French test, the visitor read the teammate’s message and answered in the same widget.


### Does taking over a HubSpot conversation also change the ticket owner?


In our test, taking ownership changed the conversation owner to Piotr. The associated ticket stayed assigned to Beacon Bot in Support Pipeline. Check Owner above the chat to see who is replying, and check the ticket card separately to see who owns the follow-up.
